Title: Maximum stored energy under 10 kWh
Finding: 546 cells x 3.6 V x 5.0 Ah x f=1.0 = 9828 Wh. Margin 172 Wh (1.72%).
Action: Margin is thin. The rule caps the pack at 555 cells of this type; you have 546.

Title: Motor nominal power at or below 25 kW
Finding: Competr hardware is rated 26.9 kW nominal (42 kW peak), which is 1.9 kW over the rule limit. The drivetrain is configured to 25.0 kW, which complies, and every model in this project enforces that limit.
Action: Compliance depends entirely on the derate. Get a written statement from Competr confirming the unit can be limited to 25 kW nominal, and be able to show the setting in the inverter configuration at scrutineering.

Title: Approval required for voltage above 100 V
Finding: Pack reaches 109.2 V at 100% SOC (26S x 4.2 V), above the 100 V threshold.
Action: Obtain Technical Committee approval during registration. This is a paperwork gate, not a design fault -- but without it the boat cannot race.

Title: High voltage training certification
Finding: System reaches 109.2 V, so the 100 V threshold applies.
Action: Everyone who works on the pack needs a high voltage training certificate. Checked at technical inspection.

Title: Fuse rating below weakest protected component
Finding: 400 A fuse protects Series busbar (90 mm2) rated 450 A continuous.

Title: Fuse immediately after the energy storage
Finding: A 400 A fuse is modelled in the HV path.
Action: Confirm the physical fuse sits immediately after the pack terminals, before any other component. Also required on the telemetry battery.

Title: Adequately sized wire gauge
Finding: 150 mm2 cable, 459 A derated, against 375 A maximum continuous draw.

Title: Batteries used within datasheet ratings
Finding: 17.86 A per cell at the 375 A bus maximum, against a 60 A datasheet continuous rating (30% utilisation).

Title: Overall weight excluding hulls under 250 kg
Finding: Pack 52 kg + outboard 35 kg + pilot 80 kg = 167 kg. 83 kg left for cockpit structure, seat, controls, safety gear and wiring.
Action: Cockpit structure is not modelled. Weigh the complete boat -- an overweight boat is not allowed in the water.

Title: Exposed parts below 60 degC
Finding: Highest modelled steady cell temperature 53.6 degC.

Title: Battery temperature monitored and shown to pilot
Finding: Not a model property. The BMS must display cell temperature to the pilot, and the telemetry battery needs monitoring too.
Action: Confirm the BMS temperature channel reaches the pilot display.

Title: Pilot warned at 90% of maximum temperature
Finding: With a 70 degC cell maximum, the warning must trigger at 63 degC.
Action: Set the BMS warning threshold to 63 degC.

Title: Pass-through hole for organiser temperature sensor
Finding: A 3.2 mm hole is required, positioned so the sensor can reach the cells at the core of the pack.
Action: Add the pass-through to the enclosure design. The three empty slots in the 4x4 grid give a natural route to the pack centre.

Title: Steering rotates at least 40 degrees each side
Finding: Competr steering range -40 to +40 degrees.
Action: Exactly at the limit, with no margin. Verify the installed range on the boat.
